fluff.overview: The Mars Assault Vehicle is one of the most formidable combat vehicles the Clans field. Developed in the 2840s as part of ilKhan Jerome Winson's pro-vehicle initiative, it entered service in 2871 and quickly became a fixture in Clan garrison clusters across the Homeworlds. Named for the Roman god of war, the Mars is a hundred-ton tracked assault vehicle designed to fill the same battlefield role as the heaviest BattleMechs without the extensive training demands of a MechWarrior crew. Clan Hell's Horses, whose enthusiasm for conventional forces is well documented, maintained the most consistent production record and pioneered several variant configurations. The vehicle's combination of heavy armor, a potent ECM suite, and a large-bore weapons array has kept it relevant across multiple eras of Clan warfare.
fluff.capabilities:
The Mars mounts eleven and a half tons of Compound Zeta ferro-fibrous armor, enough to absorb punishment from all but the heaviest weapons. An ECM Suite degrades enemy electronics within range, complicating targeting solutions for opposing units and partially compensating for the vehicle's limited mobility. These defensive advantages come at a price. A Fusion 200 power plant limits the Mars to a top speed of 32 km/h, making it dependent on terrain and friendly screening forces to avoid being outflanked by faster opponents.

The weapons array is designed for long-range engagement. A CRG Gauss Rifle and Series 7N Extended Range Large Laser occupy the turret, providing accurate fire at distances where most opponents cannot effectively retaliate. A Type KOV LB-10X Autocannon adds versatility, particularly against aircraft and lightly armored vehicles using cluster munitions. Three Type XV Crossbow LRM-15 launchers, each slaved to an Artemis IV fire control system, deliver sustained indirect fire with improved hit probability. Two Pattern J6c Streak SRM-6 launchers protect the flanks against close-range threats, ensuring that opponents cannot simply maneuver around the main weapons to exploit weaknesses. A pair of Series IX machine guns handles unarmored infantry. The weapons array consumes more than half the vehicle's mass, leaving crew survivability dependent on armor and ECM rather than the ability to disengage.
fluff.deployment: The HAG variant entered service during the Jihad as the Rasalhague Dominion sought to stiffen its defenses following the Ice Hellion raids. Produced exclusively at Orestes by Odin Manufacturing, it combines the XL engine's speed improvement with the heaviest armor of any Mars configuration and a Class 30 Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle capable of inflicting devastating structural damage at range. The Ghost Bears did not share the design freely. Trial or salvage remained the primary means of acquisition outside the Dominion. The HAG remained a Rasalhague Dominion frontline asset through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, valued for its combination of firepower and survivability.
fluff.history:
The Mars traces its origins to the 2840s, when ilKhan Jerome Winson championed a deliberate expansion of Clan conventional forces. Winson argued that the Clans' reliance on BattleMechs left them vulnerable in the garrison and defensive roles that consumed much of their military capacity between Trials and border skirmishes. The Mars was his answer, a vehicle that could match a heavy BattleMech in firepower and absorb similar punishment without requiring the years of sibko training and scarce MechWarrior talent that front-line combat units demanded.

Entering service in 2871, the design was adopted by nearly every Clan with the manufacturing base to support it. Multiple Homeworld factories began producing the Mars for their respective toumans, and the type spread across the Clan Homeworlds over the following decades. Clan Hell's Horses, whose doctrine treated conventional forces as genuine frontline assets rather than second-tier support, became the most committed operator. The Horses maintained the highest production rates and pushed the design's development further than any other Clan.

The vehicle's slow speed drew persistent criticism from warriors who viewed vehicles as inherently inferior to BattleMechs, but the Mars consistently performed in the roles it was designed for. It anchored defensive lines, supported Trials of Possession, and on more than a few occasions proved an unpleasant surprise for MechWarriors who underestimated its firepower. Its ECM suite gave it a tactical edge that few conventional vehicles of comparable era could claim.

During the Wars of Reaving, production at several Homeworld facilities was disrupted or destroyed outright. Clan Hell's Horses, having relocated significant industrial capacity to the Inner Sphere, restarted Mars production at Kirchbach in 3072. The Horses made the design available commercially, selling to any buyer. The Rasalhague Dominion secured its own supply through the Orestes facility, where Odin Manufacturing produced the HAG variant beginning in 3075. These Inner Sphere footholds ensured the Mars remained available well into the Dark Age, long after the Homeworld production network had fragmented beyond recovery.
